draft.evidence: Genesis 10:29 names Ophir among Joktan’s sons. The parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 1:23 gives the same identification.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists Ophir alongside Havilah and Jobab, then identifies them with כָּל אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי יָקְטָן, “all these are sons of Joktan.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun, spelled here without the yod of the dictionary form. The conjunction and direct-object marker form the preceding word וְאֶת.

evidence.note: The heading וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ identifies Havilah as a son of Cush.
Havilah appears between Ophir and Jobab in the list that closes with כָּל אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי יָקְטָן, “all these are sons of Joktan.”

article.name: חֲוִילָה
article.summary: Genesis 10 names two men called Havilah, a son of Cush and a son of Joktan. The derivation of the name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add the son of Joktan and his verse to the proposed personal-name article alongside the son of Cush.
draft.definition: Havilah is a personal name borne by a son of Cush and a son of Joktan.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:7 lists one Havilah among the sons of Cush. Genesis 10:29 identifies another as a son of Joktan.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:29 lists חֲוִילָה between Ophir and Jobab. The closing words כָּל אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי יָקְטָן, “all these are sons of Joktan,” identify the bearer. The verse gives no etymology for his name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun. The preceding וְאֶת supplies the conjunction and direct-object marker as a separate word. The name itself has no prefix or suffix.
